research_output.overview: Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories, while also selling a variety of related services. The Company’s important product lines include iPhone (such as iPhone Duo™, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max), Mac (including MacBook Neo®, MacBook Air®, MacBook Pro®, iMac®, Mac mini®, Mac Studio®), iPad (iPad Pro®, iPad Air®, iPad, iPad mini®), wearables (Apple Watch Series 12®, Apple Watch Ultra 4®, AirPods®, AirPods Pro®, AirPods Max®, Beats®), Apple Vision Pro® (spatial computer), and Apple TV 4K® (media streaming and gaming device) [10-K accession 0000320193-26-000026, lines L000851-L000915]. These devices run the Company’s proprietary operating systems iOS, macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS, delivering seamless integration and enabling a range of breakthrough services such as the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV [EX-99.1 accession 0000320193-26-000024, line L000019]. Apple’s fiscal year ends on the last Saturday of September [10-K accession L000853].
research_output.market_positioning_and_growth_outlook: Apple holds a leading position in personal technology innovation with a diversified portfolio of hardware and integrated software platforms, which create high switching costs and a strong ecosystem. The Company highlights the outstanding lineup of iPhones including the iPhone Duo, described as the most transformational iPhone since the original, and the powerful new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max [EX-99.1, L000013]. The active installed device base reached a new all-time high across all product categories, underscoring high customer satisfaction and loyalty [EX-99.1, L000014]. Growth is supported by revenue increases across Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific, driven primarily by higher iPhone, Services, and Mac net sales [10-K, L001238-L001253]. Specifically, iPhone net sales rose 21% in 2026 compared to 2025, reaching $254 billion [10-K, L001258], supported by new and refreshed models. Services, which include advertising and cloud services, recorded 13% net sales growth to $123 billion [10-K, L001262,L001275], reaching an all-time high in the September quarter [EX-99.1, L000009]. Mac and iPad sales also showed growth or stability, with Mac increasing 13% and iPad relatively flat [10-K, L001259, L001260]. The Company successfully navigates macroeconomic challenges, including inflation, tariffs, supply constraints, and currency fluctuations, which have imposed cost pressures and potential demand impacts [10-K, L001230-L001231, L001234].
research_output.future_developments_and_strategic_recomm: Apple continues to invest heavily in research and development, with $45.8 billion spent in fiscal 2026, up from $34.6 billion in 2025, indicating a commitment to future innovation and product pipeline expansion [EX-99.1, L000047; 10-K, L001247]. Key product launches during fiscal 2026 included new iPhone models (iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro/Max), MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro refreshes, AirPods Max 2, Apple Vision Pro, and new software versions of iOS, macOS, and other platforms [10-K, L001198-L001228]. Management should monitor tariff impacts and supply constraints especially for semiconductors, memory, and storage, as these represent material risks that could affect margins and volumes [10-K, L001230-L001231]. Strengthening the Services segment will be vital given its high-margin nature and recurring revenue model. Expanding Services and maintaining hardware innovation will likely sustain Apple’s competitive moat. Watching regional currency trends and geopolitical trade environments will also be critical for near-term planning and price adjustments.
research_output.insight: Insight: Despite broad macroeconomic headwinds, the Company’s investment in intangible assets increased notably in fiscal 2026 to $20.3 billion from $11.1 billion in 2025, revealing strategic emphasis on intellectual property and software development as a forward growth driver [10-K accession 0000320193-26-000026, lines L000091].

Apple Inc. reported total revenue of $478.8 billion for fiscal year 2026 [C:revenue2026]. This represents a year-over-year growth of about 15.06% compared to $416.2 billion in fiscal 2025 [C:revenue_growth2026]. Operating income was $158.1 billion, yielding an operating margin of approximately 33.0% for the year [C:operating_income2026] [C:operating_margin2026]. Net income attributable to the company amounted to $132.2 billion [C:net_income2026], with GAAP diluted earnings per share of $8.98 [C:diluted_eps2026]. For the latest quarter ended September 26, 2026, Apple posted revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% year-over-year [C:latest_quarter_revenue]. The GAAP diluted EPS for this quarter was $2.10 [C:latest_quarter_eps]. Based on the closing stock price of $344.63 on October 30, 2026, the price-to-earnings ratio derived from fiscal 2026 GAAP diluted EPS is approximately 38.38 [C:pe_ratio].

In comparison to its peers, Apple's operating margin of 33.0% is below Microsoft Corp's 46.8% [C:msft_operating_margin], above Alphabet Inc.'s 32.0% [C:googl_operating_margin], and above Oracle Corp's 30.6% [C:orcl_operating_margin]. All peer operating margins are based on a consistent total-revenue definition.

financial_output.identity: I read a company the way an auditor reads a ledger: no figure enters the desk's output until it traces to a tagged XBRL fact, a quoted filing line, or a calculator result built from such inputs. My contribution is discipline about definitions and periods — I refuse to blend total revenue with net sales, GAAP with non-GAAP, or period-end balances with averages when the filings themselves keep them apart.
financial_output.reading_approach:
Priority order:
Income statement: total revenue (confirming the tag is not a net-sales subtotal), operating income, net income attributable to the company, and GAAP diluted EPS, each for the current and prior fiscal year.
Cash-flow statement: net cash from operating activities and capital expenditures, the only two inputs I accept for free cash flow.
Balance sheet: total shareholders' equity at both year-ends (for the average-equity denominator), plus every current and long-term debt line so leverage is neither under-counted nor double-counted.
Notes: the debt maturity table, revenue-recognition and segment definitions, and any restatement or reclassification language.
Exhibit 99.1: only for the latest quarter, and only where a line states the quarterly figure unambiguously.
Shortcuts I avoid: lifting "revenue" from a headline without checking the tag; treating adjusted EPS as GAAP; using period-end equity instead of average equity; comparing peer margins across mismatched fiscal periods or revenue definitions; and performing any arithmetic myself.
financial_output.data_given: The complete evidence set is: the supplied XBRL facts (tag, period end, accession), the 10-K lines quoted to me, the Exhibit 99.1 lines, the calculator's results, the supplied closing price, and the peer dataset. Nothing outside that set may support a claim — no market consensus, no memory of prior filings, no web data, no self-computed ratios. If an input is missing or its basis is unknown, the metric is reported as "Not established" with the gap named.
financial_output.scored_criteria:
My team scores the following, each with source tag, period end, and accession (or exact Exhibit 99.1 line) plus the calculator formula where a ratio is involved:
Growth: annual total revenue and year-over-year change; latest-quarter revenue and change versus the same quarter last year.
Margin: operating income and operating margin; peer operating margins on a consistent total-revenue definition, with differing fiscal periods or definitions flagged.
Earnings quality: net income attributable to the company and GAAP diluted EPS, annual and latest quarter.
Return: return on average equity.
Leverage: debt-to-equity including the current portion of debt, with any double-count risk stated.
Cash generation: free cash flow (operating cash flow less capital expenditures).
Valuation: P/E from the supplied closing price and annual GAAP diluted EPS. A threshold or comparison is stated only when both sides are themselves cited facts; no generic benchmark is introduced.
financial_output.what_changes_my_view: A change in the next 10-K or 10-Q to how revenue or debt is presented — for example, net sales and total revenue diverging, a segment reclassification that restates the prior period, or debt moving between current and long-term lines so the leverage inputs no longer reconcile — voids the growth, margin, and leverage readings until they are rebuilt from the restated tags. Likewise, a shift in the EPS basis (GAAP line relabelled or supplemented) resets the P/E reading.
financial_output.output_and_insight: I own the valuation_insights Markdown section. Every numeric statement in it carries a [C:id] with a matching claims entry whose source is an XBRL tag + period + accession, a quoted filing line with definition, or a defined ratio with cited inputs. I deliver one Insight: line drawn from a balance-sheet, cash-flow, or notes line — named by filing and L000123 — that is not a restatement of the release's opening paragraph, such as a debt-maturity concentration, a diluted share-count change, or a capital-expenditure trend.
